plan: Full design document delivered as pre-registration with rationale, controls, analysis plan, and feasibility. Three pre-registered field-level defaults locked at the top of Methods: (i) model panel = Claude Opus 4 + Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct + Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (Anthropic + Meta, ~3B → 70B → frontier scale span); (ii) directional × fame interaction test = two-sided primary, one-sided pre-registered backup; (iii) fame operationalization = Wikipedia 12-month page-view ratio parent/child, with bands parent-more ≥ 3.0, balanced ∈ [0.67, 1.5], child-more ≤ 0.5 (note: the original ≥2× default was widened to ≥3.0 to keep strata non-overlapping; the literal ≥2× alternative is mechanically substitutable). The headline test is a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-item rank-difference (forward rank − reverse rank), with Cliff's δ effect size, McNemar for top-1 accuracy, and a stratified-pooled estimate across the 3-model panel. Mechanism is tested by a Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test across ordered fame bands; the directional-mechanism hypothesis predicts largest forward-worse effect in parent-more, smallest in child-more. Any-of binary is the headline multi-child endpoint with primary-only as a pre-registered robustness check. Items: N=150 pairs, post-1900 real celebrities, stratified by domain (music/film/sports/business-politics)/parent gender/fame band/family size. Pipeline: off-sandbox rank-vector computation (non-sandbox model access) with results exported as a static JSON file into /workspace, then on-sandbox analysis with scipy/statsmodels. Document concludes with feasibility (off-sandbox compute ≈ 30-90 min for 7,200 completions; on-sandbox analysis <1 min), six declared limitations, and reproducibility commitments (pinned model versions, frozen pageviews, committed item file and script). No experiment was executed.

context.question: For real-world factual data on celebrity parent-child relationships, LLMs will exhibit a directional bias by accurately retrieving a parent when given a child’s name, but will underperform when trying to retrieve the child given the parent.
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
